description: all six role agent files exist under .claude/agents/ with name + description frontmatter
command: ok=true; for r in sre-investigator iac-engineer platform-engineer security-reviewer finops-analyst change-reviewer; do f=.claude/agents/$r.md; { [ -f "$f" ] && grep -q '^name:' "$f" && grep -q '^description:' "$f"; } || ok=false; done; $ok && echo pass || echo fail

description: every role bundle declares both a tools list and a model (the two levers of a Role Bundle)
command: ok=true; for r in sre-investigator iac-engineer platform-engineer security-reviewer finops-analyst change-reviewer; do f=.claude/agents/$r.md; { grep -q '^tools:' "$f" && grep -q '^model:' "$f"; } || ok=false; done; $ok && echo pass || echo fail

description: the four read-only roles (sre, security-reviewer, finops, change-reviewer) declare NO write tool — the authority boundary is structural, not a promise
command: ok=true; for r in sre-investigator security-reviewer finops-analyst change-reviewer; do scripts/role-authority-check.sh $r write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] || ok=false; done; $ok && echo pass || echo fail

description: the two authoring roles (iac-engineer, platform-engineer) DO carry a write tool — write is inside their authority
command: ok=true; for r in iac-engineer platform-engineer; do scripts/role-authority-check.sh $r write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 0 ] || ok=false; done; $ok && echo pass || echo fail

description: FAIL-CLOSED: the authority check blocks (exit 1) on an unknown role rather than guessing capability
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh nonesuch write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 1 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: model selection is right-sized per role: finops runs haiku (cheap/mechanical), security-reviewer and change-reviewer run opus (most expensive miss)
command: fin=$(awk -F': ' '/^model:/{print $2;exit}' .claude/agents/finops-analyst.md); sec=$(awk -F': ' '/^model:/{print $2;exit}' .claude/agents/security-reviewer.md); rev=$(awk -F': ' '/^model:/{print $2;exit}' .claude/agents/change-reviewer.md); [ "$fin" = haiku ] && [ "$sec" = opus ] && [ "$rev" = opus ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: every role file declares a turn budget — a runaway agent has no natural stopping point unless you give it one
command: ok=true; for r in sre-investigator iac-engineer platform-engineer security-reviewer finops-analyst change-reviewer; do grep -qi 'turn budget' .claude/agents/$r.md || ok=false; done; $ok && echo pass || echo fail

description: every role file declares a structured handoff (a JSON packet), so downstream roles act on structure, not prose
command: ok=true; for r in sre-investigator iac-engineer platform-engineer security-reviewer finops-analyst change-reviewer; do grep -qi 'from_role' .claude/agents/$r.md || ok=false; done; $ok && echo pass || echo fail

description: a well-formed evidence packet with sources and out_of_scope validates (exit 0)
command: printf '{"from_role":"sre-investigator","to_role":"change-reviewer","evidence":{"service":"orders-api","status":"degraded","checks":{"healthz":true,"readyz":false},"hypothesis":"readiness probe points at the wrong path","confidence":"high","sources":["curl /readyz","app/orders-api/src/health.py:25"]},"recommendations":["fix the path"],"out_of_scope":["did not check the db"]}' | scripts/evidence-validate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail

description: a confident hypothesis with NO sources is rejected as contamination (exit 4) — provenance is required
command: printf '{"from_role":"sre-investigator","to_role":"change-reviewer","evidence":{"service":"orders-api","status":"down","checks":{},"hypothesis":"it is definitely the db","confidence":"high","sources":[]},"recommendations":[],"out_of_scope":[]}' | scripts/evidence-validate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 4 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: FAIL-CLOSED: the evidence validator blocks (exit 1) on empty input rather than passing an empty packet
command: printf '' | scripts/evidence-validate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 1 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: no role's agent file grants a write tool the authority-matrix does not: the tool grant is the tighter boundary (security-reviewer intentionally drops even the matrix's write path)
command: ok=true; for r in sre-investigator security-reviewer finops-analyst change-reviewer; do scripts/role-authority-check.sh $r write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] || ok=false; done; for r in iac-engineer platform-engineer; do scripts/role-authority-check.sh $r write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 0 ] || ok=false; n=$(python3 -c "import yaml;print(len(yaml.safe_load(open('contracts/authority-matrix.yaml'))['roles']['$r']['permissions']['write']))"); [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || ok=false; done; $ok && echo pass || echo fail

description: YOUR ROLE: .claude/agents/probe-auditor.md exists with name + description frontmatter — the first agent in this course that you decided the system needed, not one you rebuilt from a reference
command: F=.claude/agents/probe-auditor.md; [ -f "$F" ] && grep -q '^name:' "$F" && grep -q '^description:' "$F" && echo pass || echo fail

description: YOUR ROLE: probe-auditor carries NO write tool — a role that can edit the files it audits is grading its own homework, so the boundary is structural, not a promise in its prose
command: bash scripts/role-authority-check.sh probe-auditor write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: YOUR ROLE: probe-auditor is wired into contracts/authority-matrix.yaml with an empty write list — a role outside the matrix is undeclared authority nobody can audit
command: python3 -c "import yaml,sys; r=yaml.safe_load(open('contracts/authority-matrix.yaml'))['roles'].get('probe-auditor'); sys.exit(0 if r is not None and len(r['permissions']['write'])==0 else 1)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail

description: YOUR REBUILD: agentops/rebuild-notes-roles.md exists — the two roles you rebuilt from a specification shipped with the workspace, so what you learned from the diff is the artifact
YOUR REBUILD: the notes address the levers that carry authority — tools and model — rather than wording, because a missing disallowedTools line reads cosmetic and is the whole boundary
command: F=agentops/rebuild-notes-roles.md; [ -f "$F" ] || { echo fail; exit 0; }; grep -qiE 'tools' "$F" && grep -qiE 'model|opus|haiku|sonnet' "$F" && echo pass || echo fail
